authoritativeText.text:
本课讨论早期有线电话的工作原理。
电话筒的一端装着贴近耳朵收听的**受话器**$\textcircled{1}$，另一端装着靠近嘴部讲话的**送话器**$\textcircled{2}$。
在本课的简化电路中，电话线把一端送话器引起的电流变化传到另一端的受话器，对方使用相同作用的装置通话。

图342所示的是碳粒送话器的构造示意图。
原书这套装置的主要零件是振膜6（钢或经过压制的碳薄片），以及装在碳靴2凹槽中的碳粉5。
碳靴装在外壳1上，用衬垫4与外壳绝缘；

固定电极3装在外壳底部，也与外壳绝缘。
$\textcircled{1}$ **受话器**把传来的电流变化转换为振膜和空气的振动，使人听到声音。
$\textcircled{2}$ **送话器**又叫微音器，把声音引起的振动转换为电信号的变化。

在有电源供电的简化电路中，电流经过振膜、碳靴、碳粉和电极3。
碳粒送话器通过电阻变化调制电源提供的电流，并不是由声音直接提供这股电流的能量。
送话器是怎样工作的呢？

当我们说话或唱歌时，声带振动，引起周围空气的振动。
声波传播到耳朵并被听觉系统感知，就使人听到声音。

在电源和其他条件保持不变的简化模型中，振膜没有受到声振动作用时，碳粉的电阻保持不变，电路中的电流强度也保持不变。
图343表示送话器电路中电流随时间的变化，上述情况用图线的$AB$段表示。

空气的声振动传到振膜，使振膜振动，改变碳粉颗粒之间的接触和压力，从而改变碳粉的电阻。
电阻的变化引起电路中电流强度的变化，电流的变化反映了振膜的振动。
这种脉动电流是在直流基础上的强弱变化，并不表示电流方向不断反转；

图343中的$BC$段表示这种情况。
这样一来，**送话器处的声振动就引起了另一端受话器电路中电流的变化**。
图344所示为受话器的构造示意图。

受话器的外壳$2$中装有带两个极靴的永磁铁$3$，极靴上套着用细导线绕成的线圈$4$。
振膜$1$是圆形钢薄片，放在外壳$2$上，与极靴之间留有很小的空隙。
盖板$5$将振膜$1$压在外壳$2$上。

受话器线圈中没有电流时，永磁铁对钢质振膜的吸引使它稍稍下凹；
电流恒定时，线圈磁场与永磁铁磁场叠加，振膜保持一个静态位置。
电流强度发生变化时，线圈产生的附加磁场也相应变化，与永磁铁共同作用，改变振膜受到的吸引力。

由于电流变化反映了送话器处的声振动，振膜受到的变化作用也反映了声振动。

变化的磁场作用使受话器振膜振动，振膜再使贴近它的空气振动。
人听到的是受话器在当地重新产生的声音，而不是空气中的声音直接沿电话线传来。
（1）什么是受话器和送话器？
（2）送话器的构造如何？它是怎样工作的？
（3）受话器的构造如何？它是怎样工作的？
（4）用电话谈话是怎样进行的？

inventory.description: Tall nearly vertical dark plate at x=78..91, from the upper cap near y=14 to the lower cap near y=439. Its middle left-facing edge is continuous; the central granular chamber contacts its right side. Upper and lower end fittings are visible. Diaphragm 6: steel or pressed thin carbon sheet. Material alternatives come from approved text, not distinguishable shading. Plate remains left of chamber and electrode. Chamber meets the right side of the diaphragm. Do not replace the tall diaphragm by a short chamber wall.

Sectioned flared outer wall: upper end by the top of the plate, oblique upper arm down/right to the central right-hand sleeve, nearly vertical central right wall, oblique lower arm down/left to the lower end of the plate. Both oblique arms contain repeated diagonal sectional marks. Small dark end fittings at top and bottom have light internal marks. Shell 1. Upper and lower shell arms belong to one enclosing assembly. Shell lies outside the chamber/carbon shoe. Preserve upper and lower flares and both end fittings.

Central recessed chamber bounded by an upper horizontal/stepped dark edge near y=170, lower edge near y=278, and right-side inner boundary just left of the central outside wall. The leader 2 terminates at its upper-right boundary near (149,147..160); it is not a floating object. The diaphragm closes the left side. Carbon shoe 2 holds carbon powder 5 in its recess and is mounted in shell 1, insulated by gasket 4. Shoe surrounds the granular recess at top, right and bottom. Shoe remains adjacent to, but insulated from, shell. Diaphragm and shoe bound the granular space.

Dense irregular black-and-white granular texture between the diaphragm and chamber's right boundary, above and below the horizontal electrode. Upper cluster approximately x=87..157,y=176..214; lower cluster approximately x=88..156,y=235..273. Not a solid rectangular block and not loose material outside the chamber. Carbon powder/granules 5. Both granular regions are retained. Granules lie in the shoe recess. Granules adjoin diaphragm and electrode, not outside shell.

Horizontal striped/sectioned member across the center of the chamber near y=215..238; visible stem extends from the granular interior to and through the right wall. Alternating narrow near-vertical diagonal strokes distinguish it from surrounding granules. At the outside right end is a short rounded/lobed terminal profile near x=185..202,y=201..242. Fixed electrode 3 is fitted in the shell bottom and insulated from the shell. Stem and exterior terminal form one physical member. Stem passes through the right-side wall into the granules. Insulation remains between electrode and casing. Do not remove the external terminal or shorten the stem to a disconnected bar.

Narrow light/outlined boundary strips separate the inner chamber structure from the right-side sectioned shell, including around the electrode's passage; small outlined rectangular shoulders appear above and below the horizontal member. Leader 4 ends at the lower inner/right boundary near (175,251). Gasket 4 insulates carbon shoe 2 from shell 1; the approved text separately requires fixed electrode 3 to be insulated from the shell. Preserve separation at shoe/shell interface. Preserve insulated electrode passage. Do not merge dark sectioned casing, carbon shoe and electrode into a conductive-looking solid.

Exactly six part numbers, 1 through 6, each once, with six straight diagonal or oblique plain leaders. No arrowheads, scale, distance, polarity marks, figure caption, or circuit wire is inside this PNG.  Each leader remains attached to its pictured component. Retain number identities and relative sides: 5 and 6 left, 1/2/3/4 right. No answers or extra numbered parts.
